given.part: An open loan's `dueOn` is before today
given.why: Two loans are lent on 2026-03-02 (due 2026-03-16) and never returned, and the clock then moves to 2026-03-17.
The test clock always sets 10:00Z, so no test uses a time where the UTC date differs from a local date, and a job that used local dates would still pass.

given.part: it has no reminder recorded today
given.why: The job runs once against a fresh in-memory database that has no reminders.

then.why: The fake's `sent` list must hold exactly the two reminders, so a job that skipped the call would fail.
Each sent reminder must carry the lending member's `memberId` together with that member's `loanId` and `dueOn`.
The `reminders` table must hold exactly one row for each of the two loans.

B1's test selects only `loan_id` and never checks `sent_on`, so recording any other date passes it; the date is only pinned by luck, in B3's test (line 103-105 expects `sent_on: "2026-03-17"` for loan2) and by B2's second run.
B3 says a refused reminder records nothing, and B3's test expects loan1 missing from `reminders`, so recording before asking would fail it.

given.part: An open loan already has a reminder recorded today
given.why: The job runs twice on the same day, so the second run sees loan1 already reminded.
loan2 is overdue (due 2026-03-16) and is returned before the job runs.
loan3 is lent on 2026-03-03, so it is due 2026-03-17, which is the day the job runs: the boundary case.

then.why: `toMatchObject` on an array needs the same length, so a second reminder for loan1, or any reminder for loan2 or loan3, would fail.

given.why: The fake refuses loan1 with a reason.
The service test only sets up a refusal, but B5 proves that a failed connection comes back as `refused`, which the job handles the same way.

then.why: The `reminders` table must equal exactly loan2's row, so any row for loan1 would fail.
`toContainEqual` needs `level: "warn"` and `event: "reminder.failed"` to match exactly.
The log's fields must equal exactly `{ loanId: loan1, error: "Notifications API answered 503" }`.

then.part: carries on with the other loans
then.why: loan2 must be sent and recorded after loan1 is refused; this catches a stop only if the job handles loan1 (due earlier) first, which the setup arranges by lending it a day earlier.

given.part: The job has handled every overdue loan
given.why: There are three overdue loans, one of them refused, and the job runs to the end.

then.why: The last log entry must equal exactly `level: "info"` and `event: "reminders.finished"`.
The fields must equal exactly `{ sent: 2, failed: 1 }`.

given.why: The client is called directly with a reminder.

then.why: The recorded method must equal "POST", and the handler only matches POST.
The handler matches only `NOTIFY_URL/notifications`, and the recorded pathname must equal `/notifications`.
The content-type must equal `application/json`, and the body is parsed as JSON.
`toEqual` compares the whole body exactly, so a renamed or missing key fails.
200, 202 and 204 must each come back as `accepted`.
Only one 400 is tried, so a client that refused only 4xx and accepted 5xx (such as the 503 the service tests use) would still pass.
`HttpResponse.error()` must come back as `refused` rather than throwing.

then.part: with a reason naming the status
then.why: The reason must contain "400".

then.part: or saying the API was unreachable
then.why: The reason must contain "unreachable".
